name: Nikolay Arefyev
detail: Proposed 60% progressive personal income tax (NDFL) on incomes over 10m rubles, which is an income tax rather than a wealth tax.

name: Alexey Navalny
detail: Proposed windfall compensation tax on 1990s privatization oligarchs; died in February 2024.

name: Alexander Buzgalin
detail: Prominent Marxist economist who advocated wealth taxation; died in November 2023.

name: Vladimir Milov
detail: Liberal politician and economist; publicly opposes wealth taxes, arguing capital flight makes them ineffective in Russia.

name: Konstantin Sonin
detail: Economist; criticized Thomas Piketty global wealth tax proposal as economically unviable and distortionary.

name: Igor Nikolaev
detail: Chief Research Fellow at Institute of Economics RAS; criticized luxury tax proposals as fiscal populism.

name: Vladimir Putin
detail: 2012 presidential program proposed tax on prestige consumption which was enacted into law as passenger car transport tax luxury multipliers and higher cadastral real estate taxes, rather than a broad net wealth tax.

name: Grigory Yavlinsky
detail: Opposes regular progressive income and wealth taxes on businesses and professionals, arguing they cause tax flight and evasion in Russia; proposed a one-time windfall compensation tax on 1990s privatization auctions instead.

name: Viktor Ivanter
detail: Academician of RAS and Director of Institute of Economic Forecasting RAS who co-authored the 2013 RAS report proposing wealth and luxury tax; died in August 2019.

name: Ruslan Grinberg
detail: Scientific Director of the Institute of Economics RAS; advocates progressive personal income tax (NDFL) on high salaries and warned against taxing middle class assets, but does not support a general wealth tax.

name: Vladimir Mau
detail: Economist and former rector of RANEPA; advocates flat income tax and opposes wealth and luxury taxation, arguing that capital mobility makes wealth taxes harmful to investment.

name: Alexander Shokhin
detail: President of the Russian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs (RSPP); consistently lobbies against targeted windfall profit and asset taxes, arguing they penalize investment.

name: Yuri Afonin
detail: First Deputy Chairman of the CPRF Central Committee. Co-sponsored the CPRF bill of 28 May 2026 for an annual 1%-4% tax on luxury property, yachts, business jets, helicopters and supercars. That is a tax on listed luxury goods and high-value property, not on net wealth, so it is outside the definition. Restore if the project counts luxury-asset taxes.

name: Alexey Kurinny
detail: Co-sponsor of the same CPRF luxury-asset bill (1%-4% on palaces, yachts, jets, supercars). Luxury-goods tax, not a net wealth tax.

name: Valery Gartung
detail: Calls for a tax on oligarchs' planes and yachts and a luxury tax. Luxury goods, not net wealth.

name: Oleg Nilov
detail: Comment on the Duma agenda backing a luxury-tax bill. Luxury tax, no reference to wealth.

name: Dmitry Gusev
detail: Says only "introduce a luxury tax" in a general discussion of tax changes. Luxury tax, no reference to wealth.

name: Alexander Auzan
detail: The quote taxes "wealth and luxury real estate" if the tax concerns conspicuous consumption and ultra-expensive property, i.e. a luxury-property tax. The rbc.ru page answers 401 to scripts, so the quote could not be read either.

name: Oksana Dmitrieva
detail: 2015 radio interview asking for a progressive income tax and a luxury tax. Luxury tax, no reference to wealth.

name: Mikhail Prokhorov
detail: 2012 statement for a tax on luxury and ultra-expensive property. Luxury-goods and property tax; the ria.ru page could not be read by script.

name: Anatoly Golov
detail: 2012 hearing testimony for a progressive tax on elite property and luxury goods. Property and luxury-goods tax; the yabloko.ru page could not be read by script.

name: Oleg Shein
detail: Blog post on a luxury tax (elite property, yachts, jets and "very large fortunes"). The cited livejournal page returns 404 and the quote could not be found anywhere, so nothing can be checked.

name: Federation of Independent Trade Unions of Russia
detail: 2019 congress programme lists a luxury tax and a higher dividend tax among other measures. A passing mention in a list of measures, and a luxury tax, not a wealth tax.

name: Mikhail Delyagin
detail: Co-sponsor of State Duma bill 1153844-8 (17 February 2026): a one-off tax on expensive vehicles and higher property tax on objects valued above 350, 450 and 550 million rubles. Vehicle and high-value property taxes, not a net wealth tax.

name: Alexander Aksenenko
detail: Co-sponsor of bill 1153844-8, a tax on expensive vehicles and high-value property. Not a net wealth tax.

name: Andrey Kuznetsov
detail: Co-sponsor of bill 1153844-8, a tax on expensive vehicles and high-value property. Not a net wealth tax.

name: Nikolay Novichkov
detail: Co-sponsor of bill 1153844-8, a tax on expensive vehicles and high-value property. Not a net wealth tax.

name: Alexander Terentyev
detail: Co-sponsor of bill 1153844-8, a tax on expensive vehicles and high-value property. Not a net wealth tax.

name: Alexander Remezkov
detail: Co-sponsor of bill 1153844-8, a tax on expensive vehicles and high-value property. Not a net wealth tax.

name: Mikhail Khodorkovsky
detail: 2012 Novaya Gazeta programme: a special rate of up to 40% on luxury goods ("super-wealth": yachts, private jets) and large inheritances. A luxury-goods and inheritance tax, not a net wealth tax.

name: Dmitry Ionin
detail: 2021 speech for excise duties and a separate luxury tax on cars above 8m, property above 50m and similar. Luxury-goods and property tax, not a net wealth tax.

name: Nikolay Starikov
detail: 2021 speech welcoming the luxury-tax bill. Luxury tax, not a net wealth tax.
